a.xlink:title: An athlete performs a training session.
A verified race is a completed training session.
A source activity records a training session.
A running observation belongs to a training session.
A sleep observation belongs to an athlete.
A fitness assessment describes an athlete.
A goal review workflow targets a goal.
A goal review workflow uses a action plan.
An athlete sets a goal.
A goal has one or more measurable or milestone criteria.
A plan version belongs to one athlete, whether draft or approved.
A plan version serves exactly one versioned athlete goal.
An overnight HRV assessment belongs to an athlete.
A heart-rate zone belongs to an athlete and a versioned zone scheme.
A criterion belongs to a runner-defined goal.
Only a reviewed, verified workout may fulfill a planned action.
A planned action belongs to one versioned plan.
A capability assessment concerns an athlete.
Metric evidence concerns an athlete.
Metric evidence may indicate a capability when comparison conditions are satisfied.
A recovery review considers the recent workout and its duration.
A recovery review concerns an athlete.
A recovery review considers measured pace and heart rate as workout intensity context.
A recovery review considers available sleep observations.
A recovery review considers daily training load.
A recovery review may consider the dated COROS overnight HRV assessment.
A recovery review considers resting heart rate.
A recovery review may consider a provider recovery estimate.
Workout duration and intensity influence COROS training load, which in turn influences its recovery estimate.
A provider recovery estimate is observed for an athlete.
Running heart rate and pace help characterize intensity through the provider calculation; this is a conceptual dependency, not a reproduced formula.
COROS recovery estimates are influenced by provider training load and base fitness; the proprietary formula is not reproduced here.
Evidence belongs to one saved recovery review.
Evidence is evaluated with one versioned recovery rule.
A pace zone belongs to an athlete and scheme version.
An inferred state concerns an athlete.
An inferred state cites metric evidence.
A recommendation may support a goal.
A reviewed recommendation may adjust a planned action.
A recommendation is justified by an inferred state.
A progress assessment reviews one versioned goal criterion.
A progress assessment is supported by its cited goal evidence.
Cited evidence supports one saved criterion review.
